correctness.rationale: An exact modulo-16 eight-factor table proves synchronization at length eight. Extracting globally even positions, using p_(2i)=p_i, inductively proves unique starting residue modulo twice every dyadic length. Exact four-block comparison at lengths 2^k leaves only one repeated quarter-block B at starts m and 3m. The general minimal-absent interior repetition lemma bounds length by m+2, and differing B predecessors plus the sole available B successor give the unique maximal absent word C_m B C_1. Independent Python deck checks passed for k=5,...,11. All assumptions and boundaries are explicit.

value.rationale: The exact unique longest minimal absent factor of a canonical dyadic prefix is a natural negative-language invariant. Its forced occurrence at a boundary, despite the classical full-fold prefix having three longest repeats of one less symbol, identifies an explicit structural transition. The result is an all-order classification with a self-contained proof, not a finite-table recomputation or arbitrary slice; no claims about shorter layers or wider automatic families.
